transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (Vistara Procurement), Leila (CISO), Evan (Platform), Sandra (Legal), Rory (Finance)

Summary: quick intake to align legal routing for MSA/DPA, discuss SLA expectations (latency, availability, incident response), pricing approval path, and scope for an integration pilot. Customer emphasized on-prem and VPC options, KMS requirements, and audit log retention. We agreed to circulate a redline summary and schedule an initial performance bench.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, SLA targets and remedies, pricing approval workflow, KMS/HSM and key rotation, billing path (invoiced vs usage-billed), pilot scope, benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, um let's do intros quick. I'm Maya from Redwood AE, Jonah and Priya are on the technical side
[00:12] Tom: Tom here procurement at Vistara, hi all
[00:15] Leila: Leila, CISO
[00:17] Evan: Evan platform eng
[00:19] Sandra: Sandra, legal counsel
[00:21] Rory: Rory finance
[00:24] Maya: great, goal for today is narrow — routing of legal review and high level sla/pricing expectations and scope for the pilot. We'll capture action items at the end.
[00:36] Jonah: just to set expectations on our side, we typically support three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC/on-prem). For the pilot most customers start with dedicated or private when there's sensitive data.
[00:48] Evan: quick Q — our compliance team prefers customer-managed KMS and no plaintext logs leaving the VPC. Is that available?
[00:55] Priya: yes, we support customer KMS through standard KMS integrations, can also support bring-your-own-hsm in private deployments. there are some extra steps for key rotation and audit records
[01:05] Leila: what about audit retention — we need 7 years for some records, and we want immutable logs for access to keys and models.
[01:13] Jonah: long retention is possible but depends on retention tiering if you use Redwood-hosted console. Private deployments you control storage retention. If hosted, we can set export hooks to egress logs into your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[01:25] Sandra: from legal — the MSA had a 90 day termination for convenience clause and the procurement team is asking for a longer exit runway, 180 days. also we flagged the data processor/subprocessor list in the DPA.
[01:36] Maya: understood — we'll put together a redline sheet. can you clarify the must-haves: exit runway, subprocessors list, and any specific indemnity caps?
[01:44] Sandra: indemnity cap needs to be industry standard but we may accept a reduced cap if we can get stronger liability carveouts for security incidents.
[01:52] Rory: on billing — we prefer a committed monthly reserved billing path for predictable cost with a burst bucket. what are the minimums for Redwood dedicated?
[02:03] Jonah: reserved starts at a quarter-size pool depending on GPU type, typical minimums are 4-8 gpus for reserved, can be tuned. We'll include example committed tiers and egress costing in the redline packet.
[02:15] Tom: and procurement will need approval thresholds — if committed > $200k annually it goes to exec procurement. Anything below can be signed by procurement. We need pricing scenarios.
[02:27] Maya: we'll provide a pricing matrix for committed yearly and monthly tiers plus pay-as-you-go.
[02:31] Evan: on SLA specifics — we want 99.9% availability and P95 latency below 180ms for 1k token gen avg and 99.99% for model cache hits. Also we need incident notification within 15 minutes for sev1. Are those realistic?
[02:45] Jonah: availability 99.9 is realistic for dedicated, 99.99 is tough across multi-region without active-active. For latency P95 180ms depends on model choice and sequence length; for smaller models it's fine but for large-context generative it will be higher. We can commit to notification 15 minutes with an on-call rota if you're on enterprise SLA.
[03:03] Leila: need to tie that to financial credits in the SLA or a service credit ladder — procurement will expect that.
[03:10] Maya: okay we'll propose a credit ladder in draft SLA.
[03:15] Sandra: DPA — we have specific redlines around data deletion and confirmatory audits. we also ask for subprocessor notification 30 days before engagement and contractual flow-downs.
[03:26] Priya: we can do subprocessor notifications and limited flow-downs. confirmatory audits require scope — if you are requesting SOC2-type audits with timeboxed review we can accommodate in Private deployments, for hosted it's more limited but we can provide SOC2 report and third-party attestations.
[03:41] Leila: do you support SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning? And RBAC roles for fine-grained access?
[03:47] Maya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM, RBAC with route-level permissions is supported for enterprise console. We'll include documentation link in the pack.
[03:55] Evan: on data residency — we need all logs and inference outputs to remain in the EU region for GDPR. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[04:03] Jonah: yes we support region pinning for both hosted and dedicated deployments and private. Hosted customers can select region and force routing; dedicated gives full regional isolation. We will note egress charges for cross-region backups.
[04:18] Tom: procurement asks about export controls and encryption for exported datasets — do you provide encrypted export to our S3?
[04:25] Priya: yes, server-side encryption with customer-managed keys to S3 is standard for exports; we support SSE-KMS and client-side encryption as well.
[04:34] Rory: finance question: how are overages billed? If we do committed monthly plus burst bucket, are bursts billed hourly or at monthly amortized price?
[04:43] Maya: typically bursts are billed at a higher per-token unit when consumed beyond the committed baseline; we can model amortized over monthly commit if you prefer. We'll include both scenarios in pricing spreadsheet.
[04:55] Sandra: legal — can you share your standard MSA + DPA with tracked changes so we can start internal review?
[05:01] Maya: yes we'll share a tracked-change MSA + annotated DPA and a separate security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary, architecture diagrams).
[05:07] Evan: technical bench — we want to run 10k inference requests simulating chat with 512 tokens average across peak at 200 rps burst. can you support that in dedicated environment?
[05:17] Jonah: yes we can stand up a dedicated pool for benching, we'll need an SLO for the test and a data set. Are you providing anonymized sample prompts?
[05:25] Evan: we'll scrub PII and share a sample corpus by next Tuesday.
[05:29] Jonah: ok then we'll prep perf spreadsheet and sample test plan.
[05:33] Maya: procurement path — Tom, can you outline internal approvals so we can match timelines?
[05:39] Tom: procurement needs pricing and MSA redlines for legal to look at; then if the annual commit > $200k it goes to exec signoff. We usually take 2-3 weeks for internal review. If legal flags DPA exceptions it extends. Target: we'd like pilot start by 2027-03-22.
[05:56] Maya: that's tight but doable if we move fast on redlines. we'll aim to get doc package by Friday.
[06:02] Sandra: we may request an appendix for privacy addendum that lists data flows.
[06:07] Priya: we'll include an architecture diagram and data flow appendix.
[06:11] Rory: invoice preference — PO invoiced monthly vs card — we prefer invoiced with 30 net.
[06:16] Maya: Redwood supports net30 invoicing for enterprise deals. we'll note billing contact and fields for PO.
[06:22] Leila: security: can you support MFA enforced for console logins? Also want logging for key access and model downloads.
[06:30] Jonah: yes MFA for console, and audit trails for key usage and model pulls; for hosted some logs are aggregated but we can stream raw logs to your S3 or SIEM via syslog/OTLP.
[06:40] Evan: question about model lineage — we need ability to pin model versions and roll back. How granular are rollouts?
[06:45] Priya: rollouts can be canary, A/B, or percentage-based; you can pin to model version and we keep model artifacts with versioned hashes in the private registry.
[06:54] Sandra: legal follow-up — are you ok with a 30 day subprocessor notice and 180 day termination for convenience?
[07:01] Maya: we'll take that back; 180 day termination is a customer ask, we'll see internal legal but we can propose a compromise like 120 days or extended transition support.
[07:10] Tom: can you list initial subprocessors? procurement needs a baseline list.
[07:15] Maya: yes we'll include current subprocessors in the pack and note any multi-cloud infra partners.
[07:21] Evan: perf question — do you do KV cache persistence across restarts to speed up warm starts?
[07:27] Jonah: we have KV cache with warm-up strategies; persisting KV across restarts is available in dedicated/private deployments, for hosted ephemeral caches exist but we do prefix caching too.
[07:38] Leila: encryption in transit and at rest, can you provide cipher suites and TLS versions?
[07:44] Priya: we'll include our TLS cipher suite list and minimum TLS 1.2 (prefer 1.3) and details in security pack.
[07:51] Rory: on taxes and billing jurisdiction — we need a billing address and will likely want local EU invoicing for EU data residency.
[07:59] Maya: we can provide local invoicing through partner channel in EU; we'll note that as an option and include contact info.
[08:07] Sandra: one more legal: audit rights — we typically ask for right to conduct on-site or remote audit once per year. Is remote confirmatory audit acceptable?
[08:15] Jonah: remote confirmatory audit is typical and we can scope that; on-site is possible for private deployments under NDA and scheduling constraints.
[08:24] Maya: ok to summarize next steps: we'll share MSA + DPA with tracked changes, a security pack, a pricing matrix with committed and burst scenarios, and a perf test plan. Customer will share anonymized corpus and confirm KMS constraints.
[08:39] Tom: yes that's right. pilot target 2027-03-22 start.
[08:44] Maya: terrific. any other questions?
[08:47] Leila: nothing else.
[08:49] Sandra: no.
[08:51] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and send calendar invite for the performance kick-off.

End transcript. Note: transcription has occasional speaker labeling slippage. References shared: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (placeholder), link to pricing spreadsheet (internal), sample MSA deck (will attach).
